facts.statement: The genus Arctolepis was first described by Eastman in 1908.
Arctolepis is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish.
facts.quote: Arctolepis is an extinct genus of placoderm arthrodire fish

facts.statement: Arctolepis lived during the Early Devonian period, from 408 to 307 million years ago.
facts.quote: which lived during the Early Devonian period (408 – 307 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Arctolepis have been found in modern-day Norway and Michigan.
facts.quote: Fossils of Arctolepis have been found in what is now Norway and Michigan

facts.statement: Arctolepis is classified within the paraphyletic grouping Phylctaenii inside the clade Phlyctaenioidei.
facts.quote: Within Arthrodira, Arctolepis is considered a member of "Phylctaenii", a paraphyletic grouping within the clade Phlyctaenioidei

facts.statement: Arctolepis is most closely related to the genera Heintzosteus and Dicksonosteus.
facts.quote: Arctolepis is most closely related to Heintzosteus and Dicksonosteus

facts.statement: The genus Arctolepis includes six species: A. brevis, A. decipiens, A. lata, A. lewini, A. longicornis, and A. solnoerdali.
facts.quote: Arctolepis contains the following six species: Arctolepis brevis Heintz, 1929 Arctolepis decipiens Woodward, 1891 Arctolepis lata Heintz, 1929 Arctolepis lewini Heintz, 1929 Arctolepis longicornis Heintz, 1929 Arctolepis solnoerdali Heintz, 1929

facts.statement: The parent group of Arctolepis is the family Arctolepididae.
Arctolepis belongs to the class Placodermi.
The time range for Arctolepis is from the Pragian to the Emsian stages, between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pragian to Emsian (413.02 to 393.47 million years ago)
